races.name: AJA Novice Flat Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes (For Riders With 3 Wins Or Fewer At Start Of Season)

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: 10-year-old who won over 8f on Good going and placed again the following start, this seasoned prominent racer travels well off a lead and Thirsk's flat mile suits his straightforward front-running role; slight concern is that recent form shows a trailing-off in late 2024 before that revival.
runners_data.comment: Sandret has winning form in his recent starts — a winner four starts back and a second five starts back — but back-to-back eighths in his last two outings are a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and arrives fit enough on 31 days' rest carrying 159 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls sends him in on the back of a good trainer-14-day strike rate (1/3) and this six-year-old has an excellent record of finishing in the frame on Good ground, with four placings from ten runs in similar conditions; races prominently and the 1m trip looks spot-on for his profile.
runners_data.comment: Tees George has been a model of consistency without a win, posting two placings in his last six starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 156 lb burden is the chief concern for a gelding rated just 59.

runners_data.name: Deep Sleep
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has run seven times on Good ground without winning but has placed consistently, the prominent style suits Thirsk's turning mile and Miss Ruby Criscuolo keeps the ride; the 74-day break is a mild query but James Owen's overall yard form (5/48 in 14 days) reflects a modest current pattern.
runners_data.comment: Deep Sleep has shown consistent placing ability with three fourths in his last five starts, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 155 lb from stall nine is the concern for a gelding yet to score, though he shapes as a serious threat here.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose record of zero wins and one place from eleven runs on Good going is a concern; Miss Alice Cooke faces the challenge of generating enough late momentum from the rear in a race unlikely to be run at a searching pace.
runners_data.comment: Tropez Power has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating gives him a slim but genuine edge on this card, but he arrives winless in his last five starts and must show more than a run of mid-to-rear finishes suggests he currently can.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old is the only genuine front-runner here and has won twice on Good going over a mile, suggesting she is comfortable at this trip under similar conditions; Miss Rebecca Burley must judge the pace carefully — an honest but controlled gallop is her best chance of holding on.
runners_data.comment: Hatamoto ran a fine second last time out and has winning form in his last six starts, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour at draw one carrying 153 lb — the chief concern is a trainer currently among the most out-of-form in recent weeks.

runners_data.name: Calaxy
runners_data.note: Absent for 198 days and has a poor record on Good ground (2/10 in similar conditions), this hold-up type also carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish; the layoff combined with the form concerns make this a very speculative proposition regardless of how the race is run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning from a 198-day absence, Calaxy faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a fourth three starts back suggests some ability worth noting.

runners_data.name: Jungle Knight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won over 7f on Soft going and showed early promise, but has not built on that win in subsequent starts on firmer ground; races from the rear and wears a tongue-tie, and the step up to a true mile on Good turf introduces an unanswered question.
runners_data.comment: Jungle Knight lands a win two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating putting him ahead of his official mark — the main concern is whether 57 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Suzette
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose last win came at 8f, but in this race she is effectively pushed into a midfield berth because the rear is oversubscribed — her chance relies on a stronger pace than Hatamoto is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Suzette at least brings distance and going experience to the table, but an unplaced effort last time and a weight of 150 lb are negatives to weigh against a our rating of 61 that suggests she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form with four placings in her last five starts on Good going makes her the most compelling hold-up candidate in the field; Philip Kirby's yard has been active (3/12 in 14 days) and she ran only four days ago, so fitness is not an issue — the redistribution into midfield means she needs things to develop late to make her finishing effort count.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Misemerald makes a quick reappearance just four days after her latest win, though that effort aside she has largely filled minor roles in recent starts, and 149 lb is a stiff burden to overcome at this level.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose best recent effort was a third over 12f on Good going, but the race shape here — a flat mile at a controlled tempo — does not play to the finishing-from-behind style she relies on; John Wainwright's yard has minimal recent activity (0/1 in 14 days) and the 73-day break adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Dandy's Angel faces a stiff task here, though a return to today's distance and going at least offers some familiarity after 73 days off.

runners_data.name: Harswell River
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old has placed four times from nine runs on Good ground over distances up to 10f and is clearly at home in these conditions; naturally a hold-up type but pushed closer to the action by the field's composition, she remains capable of running a solid race if the pace quickens late enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Harswell River faces a stiff task at 137 lb from stall 8, though a second three starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hatamoto is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over Thirsk's flat mile without being harassed. Sandret, Tees George, and Deep Sleep are the natural prominent racers and will fan out behind her in the early stages, creating a conventional processional shape with a small lead group and a bunched midfield behind. The hold-up contingent — Tropez Power, Jungle Knight, Calaxy, and the four redistributed runners — will be operating further back than some would like, with Suzette, Misemerald, Dandy's Angel, and Harswell River all genuine closers who cannot all find space at the rear in a field this compact. The race shape strongly favours prominent-running types who can track Hatamoto at a comfortable distance and quicken off a sustainable pace, rather than deep closers who need a stronger tempo to generate momentum from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hatamoto Leads, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is truly run to suit horses racing second or third.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto sets fractions that are honest but never brutal, allowing Sandret, Tees George, or Deep Sleep to travel powerfully just off the pace before asserting inside the final two furlongs; horses carrying good prominent form on Good turf are ideally positioned to pounce without burning unnecessary energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hatamoto Wires The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is modest enough and Hatamoto's amateur jockey misjudges the tempo, sending her clear turning in on a near-empty tank.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace allows Hatamoto to bowl along in a relaxed rhythm and produce enough residual finishing speed to hold her narrow lead into the final furlong; her two wins on Good ground at this trip give her genuine credentials for this exact scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners set a stronger-than-expected early pace and the race develops into a proper test of stamina over the final quarter mile.
scenarios.body: Any uplift in tempo plays into the hands of Misemerald, whose consistent recent form at this trip on Good ground marks her out as the most credible hold-up beneficiary; Jungle Knight and Harswell River could also be delivered with late runs, though all three are racing in tighter proximity to the pace than ideal given the redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the large amateur field produces a muddled early order with crowding, position changes, and a disorganised gallop that suits neither front-runners nor closers.
scenarios.body: A fractured pace with erratic splits scrambles every tactical plan and throws the race open to whoever finds the clearest path to the rail in the straight; Calaxy's long absence (198 days) and Dandy's Angel's age and inconsistency make them speculative beneficiaries at best.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hatamoto's early sections — if Miss Rebecca Burley allows her to stride clear unchallenged, even a fraction slower than ideal, she could prove very difficult to reel in given that no other runner is likely to go with her.

Monitor Misemerald closely: ran just four days ago, which is a very short turnaround, and while fitness appears intact, any residual fatigue could blunt the finishing speed she needs when arriving late in a race unlikely to be truly run.

Calaxy's 198-day absence is a significant red flag in a competitive amateur handicap; if she shows signs of ring-rustiness or stops quickly in the straight, it could cause interference for runners coming from behind.

With four redistributed hold-up horses (Suzette, Misemerald, Dandy's Angel, Harswell River) all needing to operate from the rear of an 11-runner field, watch for crowding and positional friction turning into the straight — amateur jockeys may struggle to find clear daylight simultaneously.

Tees George's trainer Adrian Nicholls has a 1/3 strike rate in the last 14 days, which stands out against the generally modest trainer-form in this field — worth tracking him through the early stages to see if he travels with the ease his recent form warrants.

races.name: Caddick Construction EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Ivegate Building Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for O'Meara and Tudhope, placed twice on Good ground this season at this C&D trip; needs a clear run in a 20-runner field and traffic risk is real, but Good going suits and recent 12-day turnaround is sharp.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, Yes I'm Mali does offer some encouragement with two seconds in that sequence, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; however, a fifth last time out and 132 lb to carry are both against him here.

runners_data.name: Big Cyril
runners_data.note: 396-day absence is the overwhelming concern for Joanna Mason and Roger Fell; has solid Good-ground form in the book across six runs, but that lay-off makes it very hard to trust at any price in a field this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for over a year, Big Cyril faces a stiff task here, with a finishing record of mostly mid-pack sixths doing little to inspire confidence; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a speed figure of 91 offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Quinn-trained hold-up type who has struggled for consistency this season — just six wins from 15 Good-ground starts and recent form figures of 0080 do not inspire; Jason Hart gives it a chance but the tendency to finish mid-division is a pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Eye Of Dubai nevertheless catches the eye on our rating of 98 — well clear of his official mark — and he returns fit on 13 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the worry is that his recent finishes offer little to cling to.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's six-year-old is a natural front-and-prominent runner whose visceral desire to race forward is well established, but with County Carlow and Kats Bob already committed to the lead, this horse will be squeezed for room from the off — its chance is tempered by the likelihood it cannot access its preferred berth.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the majority of his rivals on our figures, Woodstock faces a stiff task from stall 15 carrying 131 lb, and while he won last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, he holds little appeal at this level.

runners_data.name: County Carlow
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for Ben Haslam and Andrew Mullen, a course-and-distance winner this term on Soft; will be first to the pace and sets the race up for others, but at OR 83 and three years old with only two Good-ground runs, it may find the final furlong brutal under a contested gallop.
runners_data.comment: County Carlow has a win and two runner-up finishes in recent starts, but he finished seventh last time out and ranks fifteenth of nineteen on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights off 130 lb from stall 18.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Fahey's hold-up specialist is a genuine closer by style, despite being mapped to midfield — its last five runs show consistent placing form at this trip on Good ground and the five-pound claimer Tindall is an experienced enough pilot; the 12-day return is positive.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old front-runner for Ruth Carr who will be first or second to the rail, but form figures of 407220 and a history of fading late on Good (14th and 20th in recent 6f Good runs) raise doubts about whether it can sustain the lead; viscera is there, the finishing kick is not.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Kats Bob faces a stiff task, though back-to-back second-place finishes two and three starts back show some ability, and he has experience over today's trip and going after a short 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: Varian's lightly-raced three-year-old arrives with a 55-day break but two wins from three starts — both on Good — and Ray Dawson keeps the ride; at OR 90 on the top weight, natural prominency and proven class make it one of the biggest dangers if it handles the step up to 20 runners.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and rated well below his official rating, Anyasi is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last three starts, and 55 days off plus a high draw add further questions, though he has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: We Never Stop
runners_data.note: Consistently flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a serious red flag in a race where the early gallop will be honest; Kevin Stott is a strong jockey but the pattern of 380020 in a wind-op horse suggests the fizz goes out before the line.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, We Never Stop showed a flash of ability when second two starts back but has otherwise struggled for consistency, and a trainer firing at just 4% recently offers little confidence, though he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Goldie's ten-year-old is a true front-end/prominent type in nature but the sheer congestion at the head of affairs means it is unlikely to secure that position — STYLE_FIT note applies and its chance in any shape requiring it to lead or press is discounted; Good 6f form is genuinely solid from the last 15 runs but age and circumstances work against.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Jordan Electrics arrives on a sharp seven-day turnaround carrying 136 lb from stall one, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; an eighth four starts back is the blot on an otherwise competitive profile.

runners_data.name: Starmade
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old carries a penalty feel at OR 87 and is a prominent racer with wins at this trip on Standard and Good; PJ McDonald is a key booking and if it can slot in behind the pace without fighting for it, the finishing turn of foot could be meaningful.
runners_data.comment: Starmade won two of his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, but has been unplaced last time out after 50 days off; he has run over today's trip and going before, and while our rating gives him claims, 134 lb from stall 17 may test him.

runners_data.name: Woven
runners_data.note: Dods' ten-year-old is a seasoned hold-up horse who has placed on Good at this trip before (2nd earlier this season) but the 53-day absence and recent 0-4729 form suggest it is past its best window; Connor Beasley is confident handling older horses.
runners_data.comment: Woven shaped with clear promise when second two starts back, and his rating of 98 gives him a strong case as one of the chief dangers here; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 134 lb from stall seven, though the 53-day absence and a winless recent run of form are the main cautions.

runners_data.name: Art Lover
runners_data.note: Haggas's three-year-old is a confirmed hold-up type with Good-ground placing form at this trip — ran 2nd most recently and has hood in the book; Cieren Fallon is a smart jockey and at 48 days off there is freshness to exploit if the pace truly collapses.
runners_data.comment: Art Lover showed well to finish second last time out, and a winner four starts back, but his two runs in between were disappointing; he has experience of today's distance and going, yet 48 days off and carrying 133 lb from stall nine give this a mixed look.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Easterby's seven-year-old is a natural front-end horse with two wins on Good at 6f in his last 15 runs, but in a field loaded with pace, getting to the front here is nearly impossible — real ability exists but being pushed off its pattern makes this a difficult scenario.
runners_data.comment: Manila Scouse has run over today's trip and going, and a winner three starts back gives him a form line to point to, but consecutive unplaced runs since and a trainer striking at just 5% in the last fortnight are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Topwarrior
runners_data.note: Beckett's hold-up type is top-weighted at 140lbs and carries tongue-tie and blindfold; a 62-day absence and a soft-ground preference (wins on Soft, barely placed on Good) make this tough — sim-going record is just 4/11.
runners_data.comment: Topwarrior showed his best when winning three starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going to call on; the main concern is returning from 62 days off having been unplaced on his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Deep Havana
runners_data.note: Al Jehani's five-year-old is lightly raced in Britain and was placed at Southwell on Standard; two known runs to work with and a 135-day absence make this a significant unknown, though the prominent style and Good-ground claim in the form suggest it is not without ability.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Deep Havana faces a stiff task here, and 135 days off the track adds another question mark; four runner-up finishes do at least suggest consistency, and he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Durham Castle
runners_data.note: Crisford's five-year-old has two wins at this trip on Good in recent form and is a natural prominent racer; 74-day absence is the note of caution but this horse has strong Thirsk-profile characteristics and Callum Shepherd knows the track.
runners_data.comment: Durham Castle showed a smart turn of foot when winning three starts back, but back-to-back sixth and fifth placings since suggest he's found things tough, and a 74-day absence adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer striking at 30% offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Tinkler's four-year-old is a serious contender on raw form — 2W7P from 12 Good-ground runs at this trip is a formidable record and the horse has finished placed in four of its last five at 6f; Alex Jary claims 3lbs on a horse at OR 90, which is the chief query.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Lord Roxby brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going before, but 140 lb is a stiff burden and his trainer has drawn a blank in 22 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: O'Meara's four-year-old has been consistent without winning recently (103344) but all three of those fourth-place finishes were close and on Good ground at this trip; Conor Whiteley rides for a strong yard in form and the horse has the profile to run into a place at minimum.
runners_data.comment: Veblen Good arrives here in good nick off a 12-day turnaround, and his third three starts back and his victory six starts back underline a profile that our rating of 99 ranks narrowly top of this 19-runner field; the burden of 139 lb from stall 13 is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Midgley's five-year-old has three wins from 13 Good-ground runs at this trip and arrives 34 days fresh; David Nolan is an excellent booking for a horse with strong Thirsk and northern-sprint credentials — recent 31180 suggests it goes close when right.
runners_data.comment: Novello Lad won twice in his last five starts but has been unplaced most recently, and 34 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 138 lb from stall 16 is no easy ask.

races.paceDynamic: County Carlow and Kats Bob are confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this straight 6f at Thirsk, creating an honest, pressured gallop that is unlikely to relent. Behind them, a congested prominent group including Anyasi, We Never Stop, Starmade, Durham Castle, Lord Roxby, Veblen Good, Novello Lad, and Deep Havana will jostle for the first three or four positions, generating significant early traffic danger between the 3f and 2f markers as the field fans across the track. The field holds more genuine front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Jordan Electrics, Manila Scouse, and Woodstock are true prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled wider or further back than ideal, with Anyasi, Lord Roxby, and Durham Castle — all proven on Good ground and carrying the tactical nous of established prominent handicappers — best placed to actually hold the favoured berth. With pace genuine and the prominent group over-subscribed, this race shape most favours horses who can travel prominently without fighting for position from stall one, and closers with a clean passage — but the contested early fractions give a meaningful edge to the top-end prominent types who can sit just off the speed and pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types pounce off pace
scenarios.trigger: If County Carlow and Kats Bob set a genuine contested gallop and the prominent group just off them travel smoothly into the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace from the two front-runners stretches the field and allows horses travelling prominently in the second rank to sweep past the tiring leaders in the final furlong; Good ground and a flat straight rewards those who cover their ground efficiently without burning energy in the early scrap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runners hang on gamely
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is honest but not truly punishing and County Carlow or Kats Bob prove tougher than expected through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the pressure broadly shared between two pace-setters rather than one lone tearaway, neither is fully buried early and one can prove surprisingly resilient under the weight of 126lbs; County Carlow, a course-distance winner this season, is the likeliest beneficiary given the three-year-old weight advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers finish through late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is genuinely fierce and the prominent group over-cooks it, leaving the race to those held up in the rear half.
scenarios.body: Yes I'm Mali, Art Lover, and Havana Rum are the truest hold-up types who will be angling for a clear run in the final 2f on Good ground where the surface rewards sustained momentum; the risk is that 20 runners on a straight 6f creates significant traffic and a clear passage is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield types split the field
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent glut causes a mid-race messy phase and horses tracking just behind the front rank exploit gaps at the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Veblen Good and Novello Lad, both with strong recent Good-ground form and experienced handlers, are ideally suited to threading through a spreading field as the pace collapses in front; this scenario is partially discounted because several of the apparent midfield runners are redistibuted prominent types whose natural aggression may see them press forward regardless.

watchPoints.text: County Carlow and Kats Bob will fight for the front, creating a genuinely pressured gallop — watch for one or both to be outpaced and capitulate abruptly past the 2f pole, leaving the race wide open for the prominent stalkers.

Lord Roxby and Anyasi are the two prominent horses best placed to benefit from the pace scenario, but with 20 runners and a congested midfield, traffic between the 3f and 2f marker could cost either a winning position — draw and early positioning will be critical.

Jordan Electrics, Manila Scouse, and Woodstock are all natural prominent types who are unlikely to get their preferred ground; if any of them push aggressively for position in the first furlong, that aggression could disrupt the running of horses immediately behind them.

Big Cyril's 396-day absence is a significant flag — Roger Fell has not run it for over a year and first-time-back in a 20-runner competitive handicap on Good ground means it is genuinely difficult to assess whether it is fit enough to perform.

We Never Stop carries a consistent fade pattern in the data and is flagged explicitly; any punter tracking it should be aware that backing it to win requires it to break its established finishing trend in the most competitively-paced race of its season.

races.name: Frameclad Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Palmar Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Ralph Beckett and Callum Rodriguez, solid record at 7f on Good but recent form figures of 4-4-0-8 suggest a flat spot; needs a strong pace to get into the race late and is vulnerable here with the tempo unlikely to be strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Palmar Bay shaped with real promise when third last time out, returns fit on 26 days' rest, and has run over today's trip and going before, giving his claims solid grounding; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride for Tom Clover; career has been over 6f and stepping to 7f is the key query, though his sim-going figures are solid — if he handles the extra furlong his finishing kick could be effective from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Invictus Gold has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable 139 lb from stall 2, and our rating of 101 marks him out as a leading threat in this field — though he is winless in his last five starts, including an unplaced effort last time, and that inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter; uncontested lead on Good ground at Thirsk over 7f suits his profile perfectly, and a 14/15 sim-going record underlines his comfort in these conditions — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is occasionally mapped out of his natural role but here he is squarely in it.
runners_data.comment: Northern Express shaped as the one to beat here, winning two starts back and recording a placed effort last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the 138 lb burden is the one query, but his rating of 105 marks him out as the class act in a field of 14.

runners_data.name: He's A Monster
runners_data.note: Returns from 369 days off for Hamad Al Jehani with just 5 sim-going runs in history; the lengthy layoff is the dominant concern and he would need to find match fitness quickly to land a blow from his hold-up berth.
runners_data.comment: He's A Monster arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and conditions, with an official rating of 97; the one concern is that 369-day absence, which must be overcome fresh.

runners_data.name: Bobby Bennu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's consistent performer carries headgear (h) and has a strong record of placing; Ray Dawson partners a horse whose natural style edges toward hold-up but who can race prominently and is effective tracking a single front-runner at 7f on Good.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bobby Bennu does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two runs back hints at some ability; however, he has struggled for consistency and faces a stiff task from a mark of 94 carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old has run just eight days ago and carries a clear warning flag for fading in the finish; Daniel Tudhope rides but the consistent string of 7s, 9s and 11s in his recent history tells a frank story about his ability to land a blow at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mirsky arrives on a quick turnaround of eight days and has run over today's trip and going before, yet a sequence of three consecutive ninths is hard to overlook; carrying 133 lb from stall five, he looks a hard-to-fancy midfield proposition.

runners_data.name: Superposition
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's five-year-old won over 7f on Good and placed over 6f on Good in recent history — PJ McDonald rides a horse with a genuine finishing kick if the race unfolds in the right way from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Superposition arrives here fit on a 30-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on, though a ninth last time out and carrying 132 lb from stall 6 are points against him.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Wilko
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott partners a horse who is genuinely a hold-up type by nature but is mapped to midfield due to the surplus of closers in this field; the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence, and a sim-going record of 0W1P underlines the limited ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 62 days off, Sergeant Wilko faces questions about fitness and consistency, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 93 offers some encouragement — a trainer in poor recent form (1/28) adds further concern.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) rides for Fahey; the horse has won over 7f on Good and has two wins from nine sim-going runs, making it a live outsider in theory — yet true hold-up instincts pushed into midfield by field composition reduce the likelihood of getting a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has disappointed in both runs since, leaving his recent form mixed; has run over today's trip and going, and 27 days off could mean he returns refreshed, though a mark of 85 and ranking tenth of fourteen suggest he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's consistent front-marker has placed six times from 11 sim-going starts and won over 7f Good; Tom Eaves rides a horse carrying headgear (v) who is most dangerous sitting just off Northern Express and attacking the final furlong with purpose.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Alpha Capture is hard to fancy against this field despite a tidy recent profile of three seconds in his last four completed starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight of 125 lb from stall 12 adds no help to his cause.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has run just six days ago; David Allan partners a genuine hold-up horse whose style is squeezed forward by field composition, and a recent record dominated by mid-pack finishes at 6-7f on Good gives little cause to upgrade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Brighton Boy is hard to fancy despite a third last time out and experience over today's distance and going; a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the past fortnight adds little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's lightly-weighted four-year-old ran eight days ago and has headgear (p); a natural closer by trade whose best recent form came in defeat over 7-8f — the field structure forces it out of its ideal race position, which dims an already modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Perfect Part does at least return quickly on eight days' rest and has experience of today's distance and going; a second four starts back offers some encouragement, though fifth last time out and a weight of 124 lb from stall 13 make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Majestic Dane
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's unexposed three-year-old has run only twice, winning over 7f at Southwell and placing at 7f Southwell — 190 days off is a significant concern, but if Burke has this horse fit, the youth and unexposed profile could be potent sitting prominently behind the pace-setter; Clifford Lee rides.
runners_data.comment: Majestic Dane shaped well enough in his last two starts, winning one and finishing second the other, and he has run over today's trip before, but a 190-day absence and a rating of 67 — ranking him last of 14 — make him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old carries headgear (h) and has an excellent sim-going record of 14/15, but has been placed eight times without winning over extended trips — Luke Morris rides a horse whose natural closer style is already constrained by field composition, and the best form has come over 8-9f rather than 7f.
runners_data.comment: Frankies Dream has been winless in his last six starts, finishing eighth in each of his past two outings, and ranked thirteenth of fourteen on our figures he faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip and going is genuinely in his favour, but little else encourages.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead in a 14-runner 7f handicap at Thirsk, will dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. Bobby Bennu, Mirsky, Alpha Capture and Majestic Dane are the genuine prominent types capable of tracking close behind, meaning the early order through the first half of the race will be compact but not truly pressured. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up horses — Sergeant Wilko, Our Havana, Perfect Part, Brighton Boy and Frankies Dream are all genuine closers who cannot realistically get to the back of this field in one move and will be pushed into midfield against their instincts, meaning their effectiveness late is compromised. A single uncontested front-runner on Good ground over 7f at a track with a long straight favours horses racing prominently off the pace — the race shape sets up for a prominent tracker to pick off Northern Express inside the final two furlongs rather than a late swooper getting through in time.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express dictates an honest but sustainable gallop and prominent racers sit within two lengths throughout
scenarios.body: Northern Express sets the tempo unchallenged and the race becomes a stamina-test from the two-furlong pole; horses tracking the pace closely — Alpha Capture, Bobby Bennu and Majestic Dane — are ideally placed to reel in the leader without burning energy early

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express gets a soft lead and the pace is genuinely slow, allowing him to conserve energy for a strong finish
scenarios.body: With no one pressing him, Northern Express can control every fraction and produce a sustained gallop that outfoxes hold-up horses forced wide or late; his 14/15 sim-going record and proven front-running effectiveness at 7f make this entirely plausible

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and the prominent group ties itself in a knot chasing Northern Express, opening a gap for a midfield horse
scenarios.body: Superposition and Invictus Gold, possessing genuine class and strong sim-going records, could benefit if the pace bunches and creates gaps through the final furlong; however, most true hold-up horses here are mapped out of position, limiting the depth of the late challenge

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Come Late
scenarios.trigger: If a contested gallop develops unexpectedly with prominent horses going faster than anticipated, burning out the pace setters
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong tempo would theoretically bring hold-up horses into play, but the majority of true closers in this field — Sergeant Wilko, Our Havana, Perfect Part — are racing out of their natural position and cannot be relied upon to deliver a finishing burst from far back; this scenario is markedly discounted because the horses who would benefit are not in their natural race shape

watchPoints.text: Northern Express (Connor Beasley) — if he gets a completely uncontested lead through the first three furlongs, he sets his own fractions and is capable of winning from the front; watch whether anything attempts to pressure him early because if no one does, the race shape crystallises immediately around him.

Alpha Capture (Tom Eaves) — watch where he settles in the first furlong; if he can tuck in second or third behind Northern Express on the rail, his consistent placed record suggests he will be in the finish and his position at the start is pivotal to the whole race shape.

Majestic Dane (Clifford Lee) — the 190-day layoff makes him a doubt for fitness but K.R. Burke's strike rate and the horse's unexposed profile mean he is worth tracking out of the stalls; if he travels smoothly in the first half of the race he is a genuine factor.

Our Havana and Sergeant Wilko — both are being ridden out of their natural position by field pressure; watch whether either rider attempts to push forward early to reclaim a more suitable berth, which would alter the pace dynamics and potentially compress the early tempo more than expected.

He's A Monster — after 369 days off, watch how he moves in the early stages; any sign of sluggishness or reluctance to travel will confirm fitness concerns, while a notably slick break and smooth travel into midfield would immediately upgrade his chance.

races.name: Applebridge Group Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pinatique
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer from Sir Mark Prescott's yard with solid recent form including a fourth at 12f on good ground 13 days ago; sim-going record shows no wins and no places at the top two in five attempts, which tempers confidence, and being a genuine closer this race's honest pace means significant ground to make up late.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pinatique at least returns on a quick 13-day turnaround in fair condition, and her fourth last time out offers a shade of encouragement, though a rating of 83 leaves her with ground to make up on the principals.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who will look to dictate; wears a bridle hood and returns after 54 days off for Charlie Johnston whose yard is in fair form at 6/39 over 14 days; three consecutive thirds over 14-18f in recent outings suggest consistent enough but perhaps not quite the finishing punch to hold rivals at bay.|
runners_data.comment: Sax Appeal has been consistently placed, finishing third in three of his last four completed starts, and has run over today's distance and going before, giving him solid claims here; fifty-four days off is worth noting, though his profile makes him our preferred pick at 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old prefers to race prominently and has a win over 12f on good going in current form; the step up to 14f should suit given progressive staying profile, and Ray Dawson takes the ride for a stable running at 7/18 over the past fortnight — this represents the most natural fit for the likely race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Sudu landed a win three starts back and returns after a 21-day break in good order, with experience of today's going working in his favour; the risk is that his last two outings have both been well below that winning level.

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner partnered by claimer Cian Horgan (5lb); has placed at 14f and 16f on good ground and produced a third at 14f last time, but the clash with Sax Appeal for the lead may force both into a speed duel that ultimately costs them both their chance of winning.|
runners_data.comment: Talismans Time shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here on a retrieval mission just 17 days later, having run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts and must bounce back from two below-par efforts.

runners_data.name: Mick Collins
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-stalker type who has finished second at 16f and 18f on good ground recently, showing genuine stamina reserves; David Nolan is a positive booking and Martin Todhunter runs just one runner over the past 14 days suggesting this horse is the yard's focus — better ground here than last outing on Tapeta should suit.|
runners_data.comment: Mick Collins bolsters his claims with a win two starts back and goes on today's going, while our rating of 90 puts him clear at the head of this field; the concern is that seventh last time out leaves him needing to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Hamadhan
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has a 90-day absence to overcome for trainer Jennie Candlish; sim-going figures show no wins across seven good-ground runs and only one place, which is a concern, and having to make up ground in a genuinely-run race over a trip longer than most of his recent outings adds to the risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Hamadhan is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 132 lb after a 90-day absence, though he has run over today's going before and his third last time out shows he can find the frame.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who is a true hold-up racer by nature but is mapped to midfield here because the field has too many rearward types to accommodate them all at the back; STYLE_FIT 0.93 signals it races out of its natural role, and while it has placed twice at 16f on good ground recently, the compromised position tempers its chance materially.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Arrange has placed three times in that sequence — second two starts back and third last time out — but ranked last on our figures here, she faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 125 lb despite the experience of today's trip and going in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal and Talismans Time are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over this 1m6f trip at Thirsk, creating a genuine, honest gallop on good ground rather than a falsely-run affair. Sax Appeal brings consistent placed form over this sort of distance and trip, while Talismans Time has shown enough early toe to push for the lead, meaning neither is likely to concede supremacy cheaply. The resulting sustained tempo across fourteen furlongs on a flat track should play into the hands of prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can travel within striking range and pick up once the front two come under pressure late — notably Sudu and Mick Collins, both of whom prefer to race just off the pace and have shown solid form in this going. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; Arrange is a true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield representation on the map, but in a race run at a genuine clip, Pinatique and Hamadhan will also be doing their catching-up from off the pace, making the prominent-to-stalker profile the primary beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal and Talismans Time fight for the lead and sustain a true gallop that strings the field out from early on.
scenarios.body: The front two burn each other's reserves over the extended trip, leaving the race to those who have tracked efficiently just off the pace; Sudu and Mick Collins are ideally placed as prominent types with proven stamina at this level of trip and going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pacemakers (most likely Sax Appeal) settles into a rhythm and the other fades early, allowing a solo lead at a controlled clip.
scenarios.body: With the tempo easing, the lead horse conserves energy and is never truly pressured until it is too late for closers; Sax Appeal's consistent recent record over 14-16f on good ground makes this credible if Talismans Time fails to sustain the duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Make Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly fierce and the front two tie each other up, leaving the back-markers with a clear finishing run.
scenarios.body: Pinatique and Hamadhan would be the chief beneficiaries, arriving late into a race that has been run at a punishing tempo, though both carry limited win form at similar distances in this going which tempers the probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully and the gallop is intermittently slow, compressing the field heading into the straight.
scenarios.body: A truly muddled race over 1m6f at Thirsk is unlikely given the two confirmed pacemakers, but if it materialises, Arrange — despite being a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield here — could theoretically emerge; however its style fit is compromised and the scenario itself depends on an atypical race shape.

watchPoints.text: Sudu and Mick Collins — both prominent types who are poised to benefit most if Sax Appeal and Talismans Time set an honest gallop, and either could outrun their marks if the race shape plays out as the pace data suggests.

Sax Appeal and Talismans Time — monitor which of these two actually seizes the rail and the lead at the break; if one capitulates early and the other gets away uncontested, the winning scenario shifts markedly toward Scenario B rather than A.

Arrange — despite recent placed form at 16f, its natural hold-up style is compromised in this field; if punters back it heavily expecting a late run, note it is unlikely to get the clear run from the rear it needs when Pinatique and Hamadhan are also chasing the same late ground.

Hamadhan — a 90-day break for a yard whose recent strike rate is modest (2/10 in 14 days); fitness needs to be taken on trust and Jason Hart will likely be conservative with it, which may leave it with too much to do on what could be its first run back at peak fitness.
